D016-D012_h001.question:
It’s been maybe… I don’t know, several months now that this has really started to bother me. I work in hospice, so I’m around a lot of illness, and lately I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve picked something up. I’ll notice a tiny ache in my side or a little rash and my mind jumps straight to, “What if it’s something serious? What if I’m dying and don’t know it?” I keep running through worst‑case scenarios in my head, especially after a long shift.

Because of that, and I guess just in general, I’ve gotten into this habit of checking things over and over at home. I’ll lock the door, walk away, and then go back three or four times to make sure it’s really locked. Same with the stove or the kettle—I’ll turn it off, but then I stand there staring at the knob, touching it again, sometimes going back from the bedroom just to be sure. I get this rush of fear, like if I don’t check, something terrible will happen—to me, to the neighbors, I’m not even sure. It’s exhausting, and I know it sounds irrational, but in the moment it feels very real.

    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

It’s been maybe a few months now that things have started to feel…off. I’m still dancing full-time with the company, but it’s getting harder to stay focused.

What scares me most are these random, really disturbing thoughts that just pop into my head out of nowhere. I’ll be rehearsing a lift with a partner and suddenly picture myself shoving him so he breaks his neck, or I’ll be on the subway and imagine stabbing someone with my keys. I don’t want to do any of that, it actually makes me feel sick, but once the image is there it’s hard to shake. Sometimes it’s sexual stuff that feels really wrong or, like, blasphemous things when I’m in church with my family. I was raised Catholic, so that really freaks me out.

Along with that, I’ve been a lot more on edge. My body kind of jumps at loud noises backstage, or if someone comes up behind me, my heart suddenly races. I’ll get this rush of fear, like something terrible is about to happen, even though I know logically we’re just in a studio. It’s not constant, but it’s happening enough that I’m starting to worry it might mess with my performances.

I guess this started maybe a few months ago, though I’m not exactly sure when it got “bad.” I’m a detective, so I’m used to crime scenes being filthy, but lately it’s like I can’t stop thinking about what’s on everything—blood, spit, whatever people leave behind. Even when I’m just at my desk, I’ll catch myself staring at the keyboard and imagining all the germs on it, who touched it last, what they might’ve had.

It’s not just at work, either. On the subway, I’ll grab a pole and then spend the rest of the ride kind of tense, distracted, running through all the things that could be on my hands. Sometimes I’ll avoid touching things if I can, especially in public bathrooms or in holding cells, but other times I just push through and feel on edge afterward.

At home my wife says I seem “on guard” around doorknobs, shoes, the kitchen counter. I’m not having panic attacks or anything, but there’s this steady, uncomfortable fear that I’ve picked something up and could bring it home to her. It’s not constant, but it’s often enough that it’s starting to wear on me.

D016-D012_h025.question:
I’ve been really stuck on this idea that something is physically wrong with me. For maybe the last three or four months, I’ve had this nagging fear that I’ve got some kind of serious illness that no one has caught yet. I work from home writing books under other people’s names, so I’m on my laptop a lot, and anytime I feel the slightest twinge—like a flutter in my chest or a weird ache in my side—I immediately jump to “this is it, this is something fatal.”

It’s not just a passing worry; it sort of grabs my whole attention. I’ll be in the middle of a chapter and suddenly I can’t focus on the plot anymore because I’m replaying that sensation in my body and imagining worst-case scenarios. My heart races, my palms get sweaty, and I feel almost frozen, like I’m bracing for bad news that hasn’t even come yet.

I’ve looked things up online sometimes, and that usually makes the fear spike, but I also feel embarrassed constantly asking doctors to check me. I can’t tell if I’m overreacting or missing something real, and that uncertainty is exhausting.
